sections.title: Describing People with ser
sections.content: You met 'ser' in Lesson 1 for your name and where you are from. It is also the verb for saying what someone is like: their job, their nationality and their character. Here are all six forms — you need 'es' for one person and 'son' for two or more.

sections.title: The adjective agrees
sections.content: An adjective changes its ending to match the person it describes. One ending in -o takes -a for a woman, and -s for more than one person. An adjective ending in -e has the same form for both, and only adds -s in the plural.

items.spanish: Ella es chilena y es profesora de español.
items.english: She's Chilean and she's a Spanish teacher.

sections.content: Spanish drops the article before a job: 'Es profesora', not 'Es una profesora'. The article comes back only when you add more about her — 'Es una profesora muy buena'.
